Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:239873
Court No. - 65

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 49317 of 2023
Applicant :- Abhishek

Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Sushil Kumar Pandey,Pratima Pandey
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Rajeev Misra,J.
Heard Mr. Sushil Kumar Pandey, the learned counsel for applicant and the learned A.G.A. for State.
Perused the record.

This application for bail has been filed by applicant- Abhishek seeking his enlargement on bail in Case Crime No. 253 of 2023 under Sections 376 IPC and 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station- Barkhera District-Pilibhit during the pendency of trial.
At the very outset, learned A.G.A. submits that notice of present application for bail has been served upon opposite party-2 on 10.11.2023.
However, inspite of service of notice, no one has put in appearance on behalf of first informant/opposite party-2 to oppose this application for bail.

sentences.text: 1 Record shows that in respect of an incident which is alleged to have occurred on 27.8.2023 a belated F.I.R. dated 30.8.2023 was lodged by first informant Jeevan Ram and was registered as Case Crime No. 253 of 2023 under Sections 376 IPC, 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station- Barkhera District- Pilibhit.
In the aforesaid F.I.R., applicant- Abhishek has been nominated as solitary named accused.

The gravamen of the allegations made in the F.I.R. is to the effect that on 27.8.2023 at around 9:00 am when the daughter of the first informant had gone in the field to attend the call of nature, named accused is alleged to have deliberately and forcibly committed sexual assault upon the daughter of first informant i.e. the prosecutrix namely- X, aged about 16 years.
After aforesaid F.I.R. was lodged, Investigating Officer proceeded with statutory investigation of concerned case crime number in terms of Chapter XII Cr.P.C.
The statement of the prosecutrix was recorded under section 161 Cr.P.C.
Same is on record at page 26 of the paper book.
The prosecutrix in her aforesaid statement has not only supported the F.I.R. but has also detailed the manner of occurrence.

The prosecutrix has further stated that upon shouts raised by her, two persons namely,
Meraj and Virendra came on the spot and witnessed the after effects of the occurrence.
Subsequent to above, prosecutrix was requested for her internal medical examination.
The prosecutrix in her statement before the Doctor, who medically examined her has rejoined her previous statement under section 161 Cr.P.C.
The Doctor who medically examined the prosecutrix did not find any signs on her body so as to denote commission of deliberate or forceful sexual assault.
However, with regard to the private part of the prosecutrix, no adverse opinion was expressed by the Doctor.
Ultimately, the statement of the prosecutrix was recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C., wherein the prosecutrix has re-iterated her previous statement under section 161 Cr.P.C.
Apart from above, certain samples were taken from the body of the prosecutrix for pathological examination.
The results of the same were found to be in negative.
Even in the supplementary medico legal report, the Doctor has stated that no signs of injury was found in the body of the prosecutrix, including genital organ.

The Doctor opined as follows:
"Hymen- Old torn hymen"
During course of investigation, Investigating Officer also examined two witnesses named in the statement of the prosecutrix under section 161 Cr.P.C. namely, Neeraj and Virendra.
Their statments are on record at pages 60 and 61 of the paper book.
The aforesaid witnesses and the first informant have also supported the F.I.R.
Investigating Officer further recovered the School Leaving Certificate of the prosecutrix wherein her date of birth is recorded as 10.11.2006.
Occurrence giving rise to present proceedings is alleged to have occurred on 27.8.2023.
As such, the prosecutrix was aged about 16 years, 9 months and 17 days on the date of occurrence.
Investigating Officer, further examined the first informant and other witnesses under section 161 Cr.P.C.
Witnesses so examined have supported the F.I.R.

On the basis of above and other material collected by Investigating Officer during course of investigation, he came to the conclusion that complicity of the named accused i.e.
applicant herein is established in the crime in question.
Accordingly he submitted the charge sheet dated 21.9.2023, whereby applicants have been charge- sheeted under sections 376 IPC and 3/4 POCSO Act.

sentences.text: 2 Learned counsel for applicant contends that though applicant is a named as well as charge sheeted accused yet he is liable to be enlarged on bail.

Though the prosecutrix in her statement under sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. has implicated the applicant for dislodging her modesty, deliberately and forcibly but the medical evidence does not support the ocular version of the occurrence.

He,
therefore, contends that applicant is liable to be enlarged on bail.
Apart from above, it is also contended by learned counsel for applicant that applicant has been falsely and maliciously implicated in aforesaid case crime number.
Present criminal proceedings have been engineered on account of an ulterior motive.
The witnesses who are alleged to have witnessed the after effects of the occurrence are planted and tutored witness who have been cooked up on false advice.
Even otherwise, applicant is a man of clean antecedents inasmuch as he has no criminal history to his credit except the present one.
Applicant is in jail since 10.9.2023.
As such, he has undergone two months of incarceration.

Police report in terms of Section 173 (2) Cr.P.C. has already been submitted against applicant, as such, the entire evidence sought to be relied upon by prosecution against applicant stands crystalized.
However, upto this stage, no such, circumstance has emerged necessitating the custodial arrest of applicant during the pendency of trial.
It is thus urged that applicant is liable to be enlarged on bail.
In case the applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall co-operate with the trial.
Per contra, the learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail.
He submits that since applicant is a named as well as charge sheeted accused, therefore he does not deserve any indulgence by this Court.
He contends that though the medical evidence does not support the ocular version of the occurrence yet the prosecution of applicant can still be maintained.
To buttress his submission he has referred to the judgement of Supreme court in Phool Singh Vs. State of M.P. (2022) 2 SCC 74.

entities.text: Phool Singh Vs. State of M.P. (2022) 2 SCC 74
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Since the prosecutrix in her statement under sections 161/164 Cr.P.C. has remained clear,
categorical and consistent i.e. unambiguous, therefore the said statements are worthy of credit.

The submissions urged by learned counsel for applicant regarding false and malicious prosecution of applicant on account of an ulterior motive, is a fanciful doubt inasmuch as no factual foundation exists on record regarding the same.
There is nothing on record to infer the innocence of applicant either.
As such, no sympathy be shown by this Court in favour of applicant.
When confronted with above, the learned counsel for applicant could not overcome the same.

Having heard the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State, upon perusal of material brought on record, evidence, nature and gravity of offence as well as complicity of applicant, accusation made coupled with the fact that objections raised by the learned A.G.A. in opposition to the present application for bail could not be dislodged by learned counsel for applicant, therefore irrespective of the varied submissions urged by learned counsel for applicant in support of the present application for bail, but without making any comment on the merits of the case, this Court does not find any good or sufficient ground to enlarge the applicant on bail.
In view of above, the application fails and is liable to be rejected.
